title: an-instrument-that-cannot-bite-is-refused-at-the-verdict
intention: A criterion's verdict carries evidence that its instrument COULD have said no — the observation of that same instrument aimed at a tree which does not carry the fix — so a criterion cannot pass by naming a measure that was never capable of failing.
why: MEASURED n=3 in a single voyage (staleness-is-about-this-process-not-about-disk, 2026-08-17): three of eight acceptance criteria named an instrument that could not have shown what the criterion claimed. C2 said 'grep staleness.py for mtime, ImportError, __cached__' and expected zero — 16 hits came back, every one from the module's own explanatory prose and the deliberately retained retired comparison, so the instrument was incapable of distinguishing a fixed predicate from an unfixed one. C4 said 'revert the predicate and watch test_discovery.py go red' — it stays green, because the prove-apart pair injects the staleness answer, so the revert cannot red no matter what the predicate does. C7's grep counted the correction's own verbatim quotation of the sentence it corrects. All three read as reasonable when written; all three would have passed any text predicate over the instrument string. The chain has no stage at which a criterion's instrument is executed at a moment when it could fail: validate authors it before the code exists (that is the whole point of the stage), and the verdict runs it exactly once, afterwards, against a tree that carries the fix. One reading of one tree cannot separate 'this instrument agrees the build worked' from 'this instrument agrees with everything', and the second is a hollow green — which Law 8 rates worse than a red, because a red is distrusted by construction and a false green gets leaned on by a peer.
traces_to: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass; the exit gate's verdict is exactly that proof for the chart's criteria, and an instrument that cannot bite is the hollow one. Also Law 9 read onto the acceptance criterion itself: red is the default and green is earned, so an instrument already green before the build has earned nothing. And Law 3, in its operational form — the observation of the second tree IS the measurement; without it the criterion's outcome is a hypothesis wearing a verdict's clothes.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant, transcribed: PROVED + feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8). PROVE GATE: the tester runs proofs beside cairn/devices/builder/machines/verdict/ under isolation=netns, with teeth that refire this voyage's three falsified criteria carrying their ORIGINAL evidence and assert the door refuses each by name, and assert the three replacements that were actually run pass. The hollow-build trap has a name here: a tooth that only checks the field is PRESENT would go green against a door that accepts any string, so at least one tooth must red against HEAD's verdict_error. FEEDBACK-TO-ORIGIN: the origin is skills/chart's validate stage — a criterion refused at the verdict is a criterion validate should not have admitted — and the route back is orient's brick loop (deposit -> counsel -> propose), never a quiet edit of validate's judges. ENTRY GATE at BUILDME: chart claim + intent_berth + sorted_berth. EMISSION GATE on WATCHME: the probe below armed at its berth or WatchmeEmissionRed. CLEARANCE into PROVED: harbor_master.clearance.clear — and the builder device's charter must declare gated_by or that crossing refuses (measured 2026-08-17: 27 of 39 beside-code charters carry none).
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when the verdict door refuses an artifact whose criterion carries an instrument and evidence but no discriminating observation — proved by refiring this voyage's three falsified criteria with their original evidence and watching the refusal name each, while the three replacements that were actually run pass. WRONG INTENT if the field fills with sentences naming no second tree, no mutation and no revert: at that point the answer is a runnable instrument form, not a sterner sentence, and this ticket is the wrong SHAPE rather than an unfinished one.
falsifier.horizon: The next ten verdicts written through write_verdict after the field lands — read at the tenth, or 2026-09-17, whichever comes first.
